title: Affine-to-global pro-etale cohomology bound over a zero-dimensional affine base
statement:
Let $B$ be an affine scheme every prime of whose coordinate ring is maximal, and let $g:X\to B$ be a separated morphism of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fix integers $e,a\geq0$. Suppose every geometric fibre $X\times_B\operatorname{Spec}K$, for every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}K\to B$ with $K$ algebraically closed, has topological Krull dimension at most $e$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\mathcal R$ be any commutative ring object in abelian sheaves on the small pro-etale site of $X$, and let $M$ be an ordinary internal $\mathcal R$-module [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Use the small-site and indexing universes of [def-weil-size-convention].
For an open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow X$, restriction means restriction of the ring and module to the open slice, viewed on $V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$; denote them by $\mathcal R|_V$ and $M|_V$ [def-weil-open-immersion, lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-comparison]. Suppose that for every affine open subscheme $V\subseteq X$,
$$H^q\bigl(R\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},M|_V)\bigr)=0\qquad(q>a).$$
Then
$$H^r\bigl(R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},M)\bigr)=0\qquad(r>e+a).$$
In these formulas $R\Gamma$ is the ordinary right-derived global-section functor in the indicated internal module category, computed by an injective resolution with the module in degree zero; values are in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. No constructibility, adic completeness, coefficient restriction, Noetherianity, or finite presentation is assumed. Neither $B$ being w-contractible nor separable closedness of its residue fields is required. The empty scheme is included.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral (spectral-space cohomology above dimension); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0732, lemma-Leray (ringed-topos Leray spectral sequence). proof.text: Quasi-compactness of g over the affine B gives CompactSpace X. Separatedness of g and of B gives separatedness of X, hence quasi-separatedness. The usual scheme instances give T0, sobriety and a basis of compact opens, so X is spectral.

Every point of B is closed, since its coordinate-ring prime is maximal. For b in B, base change of g gives a locally finite type map X_b to Spec kappa(b). Apply the already proved source theorem AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_pullback_eq_of_field to an algebraic closure of kappa(b). The pullback associativity isomorphism identifies the resulting scheme with a geometric fibre in the hypothesis, so dim X_b <= e. In the specialization order on X, the closure of each singleton maps into one closed point of B. Its inclusion into that topological fibre bounds its dimension by dim X_b. Mathlib identifies dim X with the supremum of the dimensions of these singleton closures, giving dim X <= e, including the empty scheme.

Use sectionModuleEquivalence to replace internal R-modules by sectionwise modules over the reconstructed ring sheaf. This exact equivalence preserves underlying abelian sections. To compare derived module evaluation with abelian derived evaluation, raise the hom universe of the pro-etale site using ULiftHom, transport the topology, ring, and module along this equivalence, and evaluate at the corresponding object. This produces a small site with homs and coefficient groups in the same universe. Injective module sheaves are abelian-evaluation-acyclic there by injective_module_abelian_acyclic and the object-cohomology/right-derived-sections comparison. Transport back through the two exact equivalences. Exactness of forgetting module structure and the source compRightDerivedObjIso then identify the derived evaluations in every degree. No assertion that an injective module is an injective abelian sheaf is used.

source.place: Tags 03FD and 03F3; exact transport along equivalences and derived-composite comparison.

proof.text: Take the continuous finite-limit-preserving Zariski-to-etale inclusion from zariski_to_etale_core and compose with Scheme.toProEt. The resulting j sends every open U to an object isomorphic to ProEt.mk U.iota. Let P be its continuous sheaf pushforward and Gamma evaluation at the top open. The source filtered-Kan-extension theorem and exact sheafification show that its left adjoint preserves finite limits. Hence P preserves injectives, making P and Gamma an acyclic composable pair.

Set F=M.X. The comparison in step 3 transports hlocal to abelian derived evaluation at j(U). Apply P to an abelian injective resolution of F. In degree q>a, evaluation of the resulting complex at every affine open is exact. Apply the proved private exact_of_basis_sections criterion for an arbitrary topological space and basis of opens, specialized to the scheme and its affine basis. This gives exactness as a complex of Zariski sheaves: any section of the kernel locally lifts through the image after passing to an affine neighbourhood. The kernel-lift is therefore locally surjective and hence epi. Thus R^q P(F)=0 for q>a. This checks the resolution on the basis directly, without identifying higher direct images with a sheafified cohomology presheaf.

Transport Zariski sheaves across the homeomorphism ULift X = X, so that space and coefficient universes agree. Apply the spectral-space dimension bound to every transported Zariski sheaf and the bound dim X<=e from step 2. The object-cohomology/right-derived-sections comparison, and preservation of injectives by the sheaf equivalence, give R^p Gamma(G)=0 for every Zariski abelian sheaf G when p>e.

Apply the already proved source-library theorem Functor.isZero_rightDerived_comp_of_lt_add to P, Gamma and F. Its Mathlib-backed Grothendieck spectral sequence vanishes outside the rectangle p<=e, q<=a by steps 5 and 6. Its finite abutment filtration therefore gives R^r(P followed by Gamma)(F)=0 for r>e+a. Evaluation at j(top), the top-open isomorphism, and the comparison in step 3 identify this with the exact module-derived evaluation in the conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03FD and 0732, with cohomology.tex Tag 0A3G (1). Direct affine-basis exactness of a pushed-forward resolution replaces the sheafified-higher-direct-image route. The proved source-library field-extension and spectral-sequence bounds are reused. Repair of return 3948694bf: the duplicated scheme-specific exactness helper is replaced by an arbitrary-space, arbitrary-open-basis criterion with explicit binders, specialized to the affine basis.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NM-37de593d9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 10 steps, the new node and every cited statement. Item statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint are byte-identical to the base copy in the NA snapshot, so the target is not weakened. New node lem-sfb-spectral-space-cohomology-dimension is exactly Stacks cohomology.tex 0A3G(1) (Scheiderer; 'dimension at most d' is equivalent to 'dimension d'). Tested on the empty space, profinite spaces (dim 0) and Spec of a DVR. Searched the DAG for 0A3G, 02UZ and spectral-space cohomology: every hit is Noetherian or unrelated, so there is no duplicate, and a Noetherian bound could not be applied to the possibly non-Noetherian base anyway. Route checks: step 1 shows X is qcqs, hence spectral and sober. Steps 2-3 give dim X <= e from the field-extension clause of lem-kun-dimension-extension and the elementary chain argument, using closed points of B and the homeomorphism clause of def-pc-scheme-fibre. Steps 4-5 compare internal modules with the arbitrary-ring sectionwise modules, then with underlying abelian cohomology through lem-pe-ringed-site-derived-evaluation-slice, the weakly-etale localization and the ringed open comparison. The equivalence node's 'local equivalences are monoidal' hypothesis follows in one line from clause 1 of sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor (strong monoidal sheafification); I accepted that as elementary. Step 6: nu is a morphism of sites because its left adjoint preserves finite limits; composing it with the Zariski-etale morphism by 03CB gives the composite with exact pullback. Step 7: R^q epsilon_* F is the sheafification of a presheaf that is locally zero on the affine basis, and it vanishes by the universal property of sheafification. Step 8: Grothendieck spectral sequence, injectives preserved by the right adjoint. Steps 9-10: the rectangle argument. All 26 declared split_report.tool_uses are generic inputs (site, sheaf, dimension and spectral-sequence tools); accepted. No SGA citation. Not a re-split item. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem proEtale_cohomology_vanishes_of_affine_of_zeroDimensional_base {B X : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine B] (hB : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum Γ(B, ⊤), p.asIdeal.IsMaximal) (g : X ⟶ B) [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g] (e a : ℕ) (he : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] (b : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ B), topologicalKrullDim (pullback g b : Scheme.{u}) ≤ (e : WithBot ℕ∞)) (R : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) [MonObj R] [IsCommMonObj R] (M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) R) (hlocal : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → ∀ q : ℕ, a < q → IsZero (((Mod.forget R ⋙ sheafToPresheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1} ⋙ (evaluation X.ProEtᵒᵖ Ab.{u + 1}).obj (op (Scheme.ProEt.mk U.ι))).rightDerived q).obj M)) (r : ℕ) (hr : e + a < r) : IsZero (((Mod.forget R ⋙ sheafToPresheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1} ⋙ (evaluation X.ProEtᵒᵖ Ab.{u + 1}).obj (op (Scheme.ProEt.mk (𝟙 X)))).rightDerived r).obj M)
lean.note: The q-th ordinary module-derived sections of an open slice are rendered by the q-th rightDerived of internal-module evaluation at its pro-etale open object. The internal/sectionwise module equivalence, module-derived evaluation slice comparison, and actual-ring open comparison identify this with RΓ(V_proet,M|V). Evaluation is derived in the internal R-module category, not after forgetting to the abelian-sheaf category. Nonnegative degrees are sufficient since a,e ≥ 0.
